questions.s: Concerning the lumbar plexus in the abdomen (Last's):
o: Only T12 and L1 supply the anterior abdominal wall
L2–4 form the lumbar plexus for the thigh. (Last's p. 360)
The ilioinguinal nerve has a lateral cutaneous branch
As the collateral branch of the iliohypogastric it has none. (Last's p. 360)
The subcostal nerve lies below the vein and artery behind the lateral arcuate ligament
(Last's p. 360)
The cisterna chyli lies under the left crus
It lies under the right crus, in front of L1–2, between aorta and azygos. (Last's p. 360)
The iliohypogastric nerve pierces external oblique about 2.5 cm above the superficial ring
(Last's p. 361)
The ilioinguinal nerve enters the inguinal canal through the deep ring
It enters from the side after piercing internal oblique. (Last's p. 361)
The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve may arise from the femoral nerve
Both come from posterior divisions. (Last's p. 361)
The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve passes the inguinal ligament 3 cm from the ASIS
About 1 cm from it. (Last's p. 361)

questions.s: Concerning the genitofemoral and obturator nerves (Last's):
o: The genitofemoral nerve emerges from the anterior surface of psoas
(Last's p. 361)
The obturator nerve emerges from the lateral border of psoas
It emerges medially with the lumbosacral trunk. (Last's p. 361)
The femoral branch of the genitofemoral pierces the femoral sheath
It runs in front of the femoral artery. (Last's p. 361)
The femoral nerve passes beneath the inguinal ligament within the femoral sheath
It passes lateral to the sheath. (Last's p. 361)
Accessory ganglia in psoas relay directly back to L1 and L2
So grey rami to L1–2 from the trunk are sparse. (Last's p. 362-3)
The right lumbar sympathetic trunk lies along the right margin of the aorta
It lies behind the IVC; the left lies along the aorta. (Last's p. 362)
Some lumbar veins may pass in front of the sympathetic trunk
A point in lumbar sympathectomy. (Last's p. 362)
The common iliac vessels lie behind the sympathetic trunks
They lie in front at the pelvic brim. (Last's p. 362)
Last's says "presacral nerve" is a misnomer
The superior hypogastric plexus is prelumbar and a plexus. (Last's p. 363)
Hypogastric nerve fibres supply abdominal viscera
They give no abdominal branches; they relay in the inferior hypogastric plexus. (Last's p. 363)
The least splanchnic nerve relays in a renal ganglion behind the renal artery
(Last's p. 363)
The suprarenal medulla receives postganglionic fibres from the coeliac ganglion for secretion
Preganglionic fibres reach it without relay; coeliac postganglionics are vasomotor. (Last's p. 363)
